# model-policy

[arc reference](../index.md) › [Lanes](../index.md#lanes) › **Lane**

## Why it exists

```tagline
The written rule for which AI model does which job. Before this lane, every worker's grade was a
private habit. Now it is a policy with reasons, and any change to it has to show its receipt.
```

# Start here

## In plain words

Think of arc as a small company whose staff are AI models. Each staff seat (the code reviewer, the
security auditor, the interface composer) is set to use one model, and that setting is a single line
at the top of the seat's file.

Nobody had ever written down *why* a seat sat where it did. It was taste. Two seats could look alike
and be paid differently, and nobody could point at a page and say who decided.

```panel big
**model-policy is the lane that wrote the pay-grade rulebook.** It did not build software. It wrote one rule (`docs/adr/0069-balanced-model-policy.md`), tested one disputed seat with a fair experiment, and fixed three small habits that were leaking evidence.
```

### What this lane is for

The lane's plan (`initiatives/model-policy/PLAN.md`) says the goal in one sentence: model use stops
being taste hidden in a file header. It becomes a written policy, so that when a later engine cycle
needs a routing table, it implements a rule that already exists instead of inventing one under
deadline.

Any change to a seat's model line is now a reviewed change that cites `ADR-0069`, never a quiet edit.

### The story, in one paragraph

*This story is an illustration. It is not a real result.* Say the interface composer looks like
it deserves the priciest model, because the seat that judges its work already has it. The old way is
to just switch it and hope. The new way is a fair race: same brief, same commit, same instructions,
and only the model differs. Whoever wins the blind ranking decides, and the outcome is written down
either way.

## arc words → normal words

```lede
Six pieces of arc jargon. Each is an ordinary staffing thing wearing a technical name.
```

```rosetta
tier | a pay grade for how hard a job is | never the name of a vendor's model; the model is a swappable choice
seat | one named worker's job | the thing a tier is handed to, for example `code-reviewer`
never-do list | the things the rulebook forbids outright | for example, switching models automatically behind your back
paired A/B | a fair race between two options | same brief, same commit, one difference, ranked blind
fingerprint | the label on every trial | which model, which prompt version, when; an unreadable field stays blank, never guessed
reject-log | a note for every idea turned down | one line, one reason from a fixed short list
```

## How the rule gets used

```lede
The policy is not a report to read once. It is a checkpoint that any change to a seat has to pass.
```

```flow
source: someone wants a seat on a different model
box: ① Free to try | any model, on an isolated branch
box: ② Fair race | paired A/B, blind ranking
box*: ③ Reviewed change | cites `ADR-0069`
labels: try, judged
out: just a trial | nothing in production moves
out: no clear gain | seat stays put, and the reason is filed
out+: clear gain | tier change, as a reviewed diff
divider: 2 | free to explore | production changes
note: Trying a model costs nothing in policy terms. Only changing production needs the receipt.
caption: Figure 1 — how a seat's model can change. | The dashed line is where a trial becomes a real change.
```

## The pieces, one by one

```lede
Each piece is written twice: first in ordinary words, then what actually happens.
```

```steps
t: Write the rulebook
plain: One document says what the grades are, which seat gets which, what is forbidden, and what would tell us the rule is wrong. Six smaller decision notes give the reasoning behind each slice.
d: `ADR-0069` is the operative rule. `ADR-0063` to `ADR-0068` each record one owner decision behind it. The lane's kickoff check must pass with it indexed.
f: `docs/adr/0069-balanced-model-policy.md`

t: Give the council a middle price
plain: The council could only run cheap and thin or full and expensive. A middle setting now exists with a fixed cost ceiling, and it was run once for real.
d: `standard` mode of `/arc-council` sits between `quick` and `deep`, with a fixed seat and call limit (`ADR-0065`). The scoreboard `council-calibrate.mjs` was unblocked without inventing a grade for the one old session.
f: `.claude/commands/arc-council.md`

t: Race the composer
plain: Three composers on the middle grade and three on the top grade built pages from the same instructions. The pages were shuffled and ranked blind by the owner and by an independent jury.
d: The owner ranked the middle grade ahead in all three matching pairs. The jury leaned the other way, two to one. Neither side won clearly, so by the rule fixed beforehand, the seat stayed put (`ADR-0070`).
f: `initiatives/model-policy/evidence/phase-02/`

t: Keep a trace of rejected ideas
plain: When the planning panel rejects an attacker's finding, it now leaves one line saying why, from a fixed short list, instead of dropping it silently.
d: The `REJECTED: <finding> — <reason>` line in `/arc-kickoff` step 5 (`ADR-0067`). It is implemented but no real kickoff has yet produced one.
f: `.claude/commands/arc-kickoff.md`
```

# The bigger loop

## Why the fair race matters

```lede
A seat's grade is only trusted if a person could have watched it being earned.
```

```loop
top: 1 | a seat
top: 4 | the rulebook
stage: 1 · A doubt appears | this seat may be over- or under-graded
stage: 2 · A fair race is run | one difference only
stage: 3 · Blind ranking | nobody knows which is which
stage*: 4 · Verdict filed | keep or change, with the reason
stage!: 5 · Rulebook updated | only as a reviewed change
labels: doubt, race, ranks, verdict
back: last -> 1 | the next doubt starts the same way
caption: Figure 2 — how a seat earns its grade. | A "keep" is a result too and is filed the same way.
```

## Where it stands

The tracker (`initiatives/model-policy/PROGRESS.md`) shows the live status and burn in the generated
sections. In words: the lane's four phases are closed, and the cycle finished well inside its
three-day budget. Its own note says that time was mostly agents working in parallel, so it cannot be
compared fairly with earlier cycles.

What it did not settle is on record too. The race measured no cost (arc has no way to read cost per
item yet), and it ran with tight instructions, so it says nothing about open-ended work. The
`ADR-0070` note says to re-run the same race if a looser brief leaves the owner unhappy with the
composer's craft.

## What is next

Nothing is running now. A new cycle would start with `/arc-kickoff --lane model-policy`. Until then,
a later engine cycle inherits `ADR-0069`. The tracker flags one clash for that cycle to sort out: a
planned routing ladder has an automatic switching step, and the rulebook forbids automatic switching.
A later decision from the engine lane, `ADR-0212`, amends parts of the policy for agent runtimes.

*Cycle 5 · model-policy "Balanced Model Policy"*
